title: IDG-SW3 Cell Culture in a Three-Dimensional Extracellular Matrix
protocol: Place all reagents and centrifuge tubes on ice.
Slowly pipette 0.48 mL of collagen I (5 mg/mL) into a sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube kept on ice.
Add 0.1 mL of 10x minimum essential medium (MEM) with phenol red to the tube.
Mix well by pipetting up and down gently.
Adjust the pH using an appropriate volume of 7.5% NaHCO3, aiming for a phenol red indicator color change to orange.
Add ddH2O to bring the final volume to 1 mL.
Mix well by pipetting gently up and down to prepare for use.
Slowly pipette 0.9 mL of basement membrane matrix into a new 15 mL centrifuge tube on the ice.
Culture IDG-SW3 cells in a T25 flask with 4 mL of complete medium (alpha-MEM containing 10% FBS) supplemented with 50 U/mL INF-γ at 33 °C until reaching 90% confluency.
Remove and discard the culture medium from the confluent IDG-SW3 cells.
Wash the IDG-SW3 cells once with PBS using a pipette.
Digest the washed IDG-SW3 cells with 0.5 mL of trypsin-EDTA at 37 °C for 30 s.
Inactivate trypsin by adding 3.5 mL of complete medium to the cell suspension.
Transfer the 4 mL cell suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the IDG-SW3 cell pellet in 1 mL of complete medium on ice.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Adjust the final cell density to 4 × 10^5 cells/mL with complete medium.
Add 0.1 mL of prepared cell suspension to 0.9 mL of extracellular matrix from step 2.1.
Mix well by pipetting gently up and down.
Mix well the two mixtures from step 2.6 and step 1.4 to 2 mL by pipetting up and down on ice.
Pipette 0.5 mL of the final mixture into each well (four wells of a 24-well plate).
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h to form a cell-gel mixture.
Add 0.5 mL of osteogenic medium to the cell-gel mixture in each well to start the osteogenic differentiation at 37 °C.
Consider this as Day 0.
Every 2 days, replace half the medium with fresh osteogenic medium maintained at 37 °C.
Continue the culturing for 35 days.
Remove the calcein AM stock solution and EthD-1 stock solution from the freezer.
Allow them to warm to room temperature on Day 1 and Day 7 of the culture.
Add 4 μL of the 2 mM EthD-1 stock solution to 2 mL of Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (D-PBS).
Add 5 μL of the 4 mM calcein AM stock solution to 2 mL of D-PBS.
Mix well to prepare approximately 2 µM calcein AM and 4 µM EthD-1 working solutions.
Pipette 0.5 mL of the working solution into the wells in a 24-well plate.
Incubate for 30-45 min at room temperature to stain the cell-gel matrix.
Add approximately 0.5 mL of fresh D-PBS to a new 35 mm glass-bottom culture dish.
Cover the dish to prevent contamination or drying of the samples.
Carefully transfer the stained cell-gel matrix into the 35 mm culture dish using elbow-tipped forceps.
Avoid damaging or shearing the cell-gel matrix during transfer.
Place the 35 mm dish on the stage of a laser confocal fluorescence microscope.
Select regions of the cell-gel matrix to be scanned through the eyepiece using a 10x objective.
Set the optical filters for viewing calcein as green and EthD-1 as red.
Select "line mode" for scanning.
Set the pinhole to 2 µm.
Choose an image resolution of 1,024 pixels x 1,024 pixels.
Select a data depth of 8 bit.
Use sequential line scanning with optimal laser and detector settings.
Keep minimal laser energy to avoid photobleaching.
Define top and bottom positions of the cell-gel matrix by focusing through the sample while continuously scanning.
Select desired scanning frame.
Start scanning from top to bottom to generate a gallery of images.
Remove culturing medium on Day 1, Day 7, Day 21, and Day 35 of culture.
Wash gels in the plate twice with D-PBS.
Add 0.5 mL of 4% (v/v) paraformaldehyde in D-PBS to fix cell-gel matrix for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove the paraformaldehyde in the well.
Wash the cell-gel matrix two more times with D-PBS in the plate.
Leave 0.5 mL of D-PBS in each well for imaging.
Place the plate on the stage and select the optimal position through the eyepiece using a 0.5x objective.
Image the full-field view of the cell-gel matrix in the plate individually using "automatic exposure" under the bright field.
Check whether the liquid nitrogen is sufficient on Day 35 of the culture.
Start the XRF system.
Open the sample room and transfer the gels with elbow-tipped forceps from the plate to the middle of the sample stage of the instrument.
Close the sample room and wait for 30 min before use.
Set the "Exposure time" to 35 ms, the "Spectrum range" to 0-40 keV, and the "Electric current" to 770 µA for acquisition setup.
Choose three to five scanning sites for analysis by moving the sample stage.
Select the elements (Ca and P) for detection.
Start the detection and export the results.
Remove the culturing medium on Day 1, Day 7, Day 21, Day 28, and Day 35 of the culture.
Wash the cell-gel matrix twice with ice-cold D-PBS in the plate.
Transfer the gels to a 2.0 mL tube using elbow-tipped forceps.
Place one gel per tube.
Add 1 mL of phenol-chloroform and two sterile stainless-steel beating beads (4 mm) into each tube.
Symmetrically place the tubes into the prechilled sample slot of the mechanical beating homogenizer.
Set the beating to a frequency of 55 Hz and an amplitude of 1 cm for 1 min with a 10 s pause, repeating six cycles in total.
Start the bead-beating process.
Extract the total RNA from the cell-gel matrix using the phenol-chloroform-isoamyl alcohol method.
Reverse-transcribe 2 µg of total RNA to cDNA with random hexamer primers.
Design primers targeting β-actin, Pdpn, Dmp1, Sost, and Fgf23 for real-time PCR.
Place the tube on a thermocycler with the heated lid set to 105°C.

Perform PCR amplification using the following cycling settings: initial denaturation at 95°C for 5 min, followed by 35 cycles of denaturation at 95°C for 5 s and annealing/extension at 60°C for 30 s, with a final extension step at 60°C for 30 s.
Analyze the fold changes using the ΔΔCt method.
